doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

title: His parents and 'bippity bop'
summary: His parents supported him and bought his instruments; his father's 'bippity bop' remark shows new music is not meant for the older generation.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That’s good. Were they eventually pretty supportive of your musical endeavors?
Yes they were. They were always supportive. They always encouraged me to practice, to work hard. They bought every instrument that I owned until I was 21.
I think you mentioned something about your father listening to you practicing the new music?
Well he heard me playing the new music with a group, and he said, “what is that bippity bop?”
Bippity bop. Well he wasn’t far from wrong, right? He got the bop right.
Right, he got the bop right. I wish I had asked him to spell bippity bop, that might have a new movement going.
But you also said something I think is very important, in that you wanted to tell him — he said I don’t understand it?
And you wanted to tell him that he wasn’t supposed to be able to understand it.
Yeah it was not for him to understand because, you know, wrong generation.
This is for us, the youngins.
Seems like that keeps going on and on, every generation, right?
Yeah, actually it does, it does. It’s an inevitable fact I think of our existence.
